cv.q: What is the difference between a CV and a resume?
cv.a: In India, the UK, Europe and many other regions the two words are used for the same document. In the US a resume is usually one page, while a CV can run longer and is common for academic roles. Prime Resume AI writes a clean, single-column, ATS-friendly document you can use for either.

cv.q: Will the AI make things up?
cv.a: No. It only rewrites the details you enter. Employers, job titles, dates, degrees, certifications, languages and numbers are always kept exactly as you typed them, and anything the AI adds that you did not provide is removed automatically.

Yes. The layout is one column with standard headings and real, selectable text. There are no tables, icons, photos or skill-rating bars that confuse applicant tracking systems. No tool can promise to pass every ATS, so the builder also lists tips and anything missing from your details.

cv.q: Can I build a CV as a fresher?
cv.a: Yes. Choose "Fresher" and the CV leads with education, internships, projects and skills. Choose "Experienced" and your work history comes first.
You can create an account and try the CV builder for free.

matcher.q: How does the resume job description matcher work?
matcher.a: It pulls the most important skills, tools and phrases out of the job post, then checks how often each one appears in your resume. Keywords found twice or more are strong, found once are weak, and not found are missing. Matching is on wording, the way a keyword scanner sees your resume.

matcher.q: Is my resume uploaded or stored?
matcher.a: No. The comparison runs in your browser. Your resume text and the job description are not sent to our servers by this tool.

matcher.q: Should I add every missing keyword?
matcher.a: No. Add a keyword only if it is true for you, and put it where you really used it: in your skills list, or better, in a bullet point that shows the result. Copying a job post into your resume makes it worse, and can cost you at interview.

matcher.q: What is a good match score?
matcher.a: There is no official pass mark. As a rough guide, 60% or more of the important terms present means your resume speaks the same language as the job. A low score for a role you are really qualified for usually means you describe your skills with different words.

matcher.q: Does this replace an ATS check?
matcher.a: No. This checks keyword match against one job. An ATS check also looks at formatting and structure. Use both: this page for the job match, then the free ATS checker for the layout.

hire.a: Office and corporate staff, factory and plant workers, skilled tradespeople such as electricians, welders, plumbers and drivers, and daily wage workers. It works in any country, from India, the UK, the US and Canada to Australia, the Gulf and across Africa.

hire.q: Who can see my profile if I mark myself as available?
hire.a: Only employers we approved. They see your trade, experience, area, expected pay and when you can start. Your name, email and phone number stay hidden until you accept a request.

hire.q: Do I have to pay anything?
hire.a: No. Listing yourself and answering employers is free. Employers must promise never to charge workers, and you should never pay anyone to get a job. Report any job that asks for money.

An approved employer sends you a message through the site and you get an email. You can accept, decline, or decline and block them. If you accept you choose whether to share your phone, WhatsApp and email.

Every employer gives a phone number and either a company website or a registration number. A personal email such as Gmail is accepted only with a registration number. An admin approves each employer, and each job post is reviewed before it goes live.

hire.q: Can I hide my profile again?
hire.a: Yes. Switch "Available to work" off at any time, or remove your profile completely.
